historical_references.reference: Qala'at al-Qulaib was a major stronghold and port city in the Persian Gulf during the early Islamic period. It was a significant trade center and served as a strategic military base for the early Islamic military campaigns in the region. The city was taken by the Rashidun caliph Al-Harith ibn Abi Shamah in 631 AD and became an important part of the expanding Islamic empire.

The Fort of Qala'at al-Qulaib, also known as Al-Qusayr, was a historic fortress located in modern-day Kuwait. It was built by the Umayyad Caliph Al-Walid I in the late 7th century AD as part of a series of fortifications along the Arabian Gulf coast to protect the Islamic empire from external threats. The fortress was significantly expanded and fortified during the Abbasid period, and it served as an important military and administrative center until its destruction in the 13th century AD.
